https://aa.com.tr/en/world/netanyahu-fli.text: World Features Netanyahu flight through Europe raises questions over ICC obligations of Rome Statute states - International law expert says Greece, Italy, France remain bound by Rome Statute obligations despite allowing Israeli premier’s aircraft to cross their airspace Selman Aksunger and Fatma Zehra Solmaz 30 July 2026 • Update : 31 July 2026 HOLLANDA Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s aircraft crossed the airspace of Greece, Italy and France on its way to the US despite an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant, raising questions over the three Rome Statute states parties’ obligations to the court. "Granting Netanyahu transit permission on the grounds of 'diplomatic necessity' does not exempt these countries from their obligations under the Rome Statute," Abdurrahman Erol, an international law expert at Istanbul Medeniyet University, said. He said ICC precedent decisions concerning Hungary, Mongolia and Italy make clear that neither diplomatic necessity nor head-of-state immunity justifies non-compliance with the court's arrest warrants. The ICC issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant on Nov. 21, 2024, over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Gaza Strip. Since then, Netanyahu’s aircraft has repeatedly crossed the airspace of Rome Statute states parties during visits to the US. States have authority over foreign aircraft in their airspace Erol said Articles 86, 88 and 89 of the Rome Statute require states parties to fully cooperate with the ICC, including carrying out arrest and surrender requests, making compliance with ICC warrants a binding legal obligation rather than a matter of discretion. He recalled that the ICC has previously found Hungary, Mongolia and Italy in breach of their obligations for failing to execute arrest warrants and, in some cases, referred them to the Assembly of States Parties (ASP). According to Erol, the argument that Netanyahu’s aircraft merely crossed the airspace of Greece, Italy and France without landing does not remove questions over their legal responsibilities. He said states exercise sovereignty over their airspace and foreign state aircraft require authorization to enter or fly over it. "The referral processes faced by Hungary, Mongolia and Italy for failing to execute ICC arrest warrants stand as a reminder that Greece, Italy and France could face similar proceedings on the same legal grounds," he added. news_share news_share_description subscription_contact subscription LATEST NEWS All Egypt denies link to ship targeted off Yemen, condemns Red Sea attacks 2 killed, 15 injured in Houthi drone attack in eastern Yemen With half of FIFA confederations revolting, can Infantino survive? https://www.foodsafetynews.com/2026/09/d.text: Sign Up for Free FSN Weekly Newsletter outbreaks Dozens of food poisoning cases reported among wedding guests A separate outbreak occurred at a school By News Desk Published: September 29, 2026, 12:01 am | Share Share to X Share to Bluesky Share to Facebook Share to LinkedIn Share by email Authorities in Romania are investigating reports of food poisoning at a wedding. The National Sanitary, Veterinary and Food Safety Authority (ANSVSA) and inspectors from DSVSA Sibiu carried out checks at Brukenthal Palace in Avrig this past week. Officials became aware of the incident after several people complained of symptoms matching possible food poisoning. During a private event held at Brukenthal Palace, attended by 80 guests, 30 people were medically assisted. Of these, 20 went to the hospital for further treatment. Samples have been taken to see if food prepared and served during the event is responsible for the illnesses. ANSVSA said that, at this stage, there is only a suspicion of food poisoning and establishing the cause and the possible link between food products consumed and the symptoms of affected people will be carried out through epidemiological investigations and laboratory analyses. Dr. Alexandru Bociu, president of ANSVSA, said food safety and protecting consumer health are a priority for the agency. “DSVSA Sibiu inspectors are acting with maximum efficiency to identify the causes of this incident, and legal measures will be ordered as soon as the checks are completed." Following the controls carried out, non-conformities were found and inspectors of DSVSA Sibiu issued an order to suspend activities and applied a sanction of 30,000 lei ($6,500). The fine was for deficiencies regarding hygiene conditions, the marketing and use of food products without proper identification, and for the failure to maintain production and storage spaces. DSVSA Sibiu officers also ordered the official detention of 15.6-kilograms of food products. Illnesses at school Earlier in September, operations at a catering company linked to an outbreak at a school were suspended. The suspected food poisoning at Căiuți Middle School, Bacău County was noted by ANSVSA and DSVSA Bacău inspectors. A total of 26 children with symptoms were reported, all students at the school, and an 8-year-old child was hospitalized. Students who fell ill consumed pasta with tomato sauce, chicken and apple as part of a meal program. Food was provided by a catering unit in Vrancea County, in the municipality of Adjud. Following non-conformities detected at the site that prepared and delivered the food products, authorities ordered the suspension of activities and applied a sanction of 65,000 lei ($14,000). Dr. Alexandru Bociu said there is no room for compromise when it comes to the safety of food intended for children. “The suspension of activity and the sanction applied in this case are measures that reflect the seriousness of the non-conformities found. At the same time, we must be very careful not to draw conclusions before all analyses are completed. Our priority is the health of children and the accurate identification of the causes that led to this situation." https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/10/20/izra.text: Menü Kereső Budapesten fogadta Jichák Hercog izraeli elnököt Magyar Péter Belföld Nádor András Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Budapesten fogadta Magyar Péter az izraeli elnököt, Jichák Hercogot – jelentette be a Facebookon a magyar miniszterelnök. „Egyetértettünk abban, hogy mindannyiunk érdeke az Izrael és Magyarország között meglévő szoros történelmi, kulturális, gazdasági és védelmi együttműködés további erősítése” – írta Magyar Péter, aki örömmel elfogadta Hercog meghívását egy izraeli látogatásra. Hercog kedden tárgyalt Baka András köztársasági elnökkel is. Az MTI szerint a tárgyalás után azt mondta, a magyar és izraeli nép is tudja, hogy a szabadság nincs ingyen, de érdemes küzdeni érte, még ha magas is az ára. A köztársasági elnökkel közösen tett sajtónyilatkozatában arról is beszélt, hogy Magyarország mindig is fontos szövetségese és barátja volt Izraelnek. Hercog szerint a magyarok 1956-ban letépték a zsarnokság jelképét a zászlójukról és harcoltak a szabadságért, a szuverenitásért. Azt mondta, Magyarországhoz hasonlóan az állandó terrorfenyegetettségben élő Izraelt is megtanította a történelem arra, hogy a szabadság nincs ingyen. Magyar Péter korábban, a Tisza győzelmével zárult áprilisi választás után még a nemzetközi körözés alatt álló Benjámin Netanjahu izraeli miniszterelnököt hívta Budapestre. Netanjahu nemzetközi megítélése a gázai háború kitörése óta nem a legpozitívabb. A főleg európai, latin-amerikai és afrikai országokat tömörítő Nemzetközi Büntetőbíróság (ICC) 2024 októberében adott ki vele szemben elfogatóparancsot , amely szerint emberiesség elleni bűncselekményekkel, így szándékos éheztetés háborús eszközként való felhasználásával, a polgári lakosság elleni szándékos támadásnak minősülő háborús bűnökkel és gyilkossággal vádolják.
